settings.events_tag_help: Pick the tag you use for events. Discussions started in this tag get a "When?" date and time box in the composer. Once a discussion has a date, it shows on the calendar page (/events) and its starter can add an attendee list. The date is optional unless you turn on the setting below; a discussion in this tag without a date is just a normal discussion. Discussions in other tags aren't affected. The "Post Event" button on the calendar page starts a discussion in this tag.
settings.go_heading: When an event has enough attendees
settings.go_help: Hosts can set a minimum number of attendees for an event to go ahead. Once enough have confirmed, the attendee list shows this message. You can use '{Event}', '{event}', '{Attendees}' and the other wording placeholders. Leave it empty for the default.
settings.waitlist_enabled_help: When this is on, each event's attendee list can have a wait list for when it's full, and hosts can still turn it off for their own event. When it's off, no event has a wait list. Once every spot is taken nobody else can join, and the wait list options are hidden. People already on a wait list stay listed until the host moves or removes them.
settings.require_date: Every event must have a date and time
settings.require_date_help: When this is on, a new discussion in the events tag can't be posted until "When?" is filled in, and an event's date can be changed but not removed. Discussions that already exist without a date aren't changed.
settings.who_help: Who can post events: anyone who can start a discussion in the events tag can post an event. To limit it to certain groups, go to Permissions, restrict the events tag, and choose who can "Start discussions" in it. Viewing and replying work the same way, through the tag's own permissions.
settings.words_help: What your forum calls these things. Every button, label, notification and email uses them. Leave a box empty for the default shown in it.
